newsitem.title: FRANCE: Bomb explodes outside government building in Paris.
newsitem.headline: Bomb explodes outside government building in Paris.

text.p: A bomb exploded outside a government building in the inner Paris suburbs early on Monday causing medium damage but no casualties, radio France-Info said.
The attack was against the headquarters of the INSEE national statistics institute building at Malakoff, adjacent to Paris's main ring road, the radio quoted police as saying.
The blast blew out a main door to the building and some windows in nearby blocks of flats, the radio said.

No one claimed responsibility for the attack. Specialists said the detonating of a bomb outside a government building at an hour when it was unlikely to cause casualties bore the characteristics of Corsican separatist guerrillas who have started carrying out actions on the French mainland.

Security forces throughout the country are on alert for possible attacks both by Corsican separatists and by Moslem extremists. A bomb attack blamed on Algerian Moslem rebels killed four people on a Paris commuter train earlier this month.
On Saturday, police defused a bomb hidden in a plastic bag and planted in a busy central post office in the Mediterranean port of Marseille.

The outlawed Corsican National Liberation Front (FLNC)-Historic Wing, has threatened to step up its campaign on the mainland after the arrest of Corsica's best-known separatist leader who was remanded in custody in Paris last week.
Francois Santoni, head of Cuncolta Naziunalista, the FLNC's legal wing, and his lawyer girlfriend Marie-Helene Mattei were placed under investigation for attempted extortion and bomb attacks.
